offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine with default stipulation
number_of_offences: Five accused persons were originally tried, but only the appellant was finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found meticulous planning and conspiracy to commit murder
motive: To eliminate Mirwaiz Moulvi Farooq, viewed as an agent of the Indian Government working against militant groups
key_evidence_accepted: The confession made by the accused was voluntary and truthful and hence reliable. The confessional statement was also corroborated by oral and documentary evidence.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, with the prosecution being able to prove the homicidal death of the deceased and the involvement of the accused persons.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant-accused was arrested in Delhi in some other case and later arrested in the instant case. He did not abscond but was apprehended.

legal_representation.accused: Sushil Kumar, Aditya Kumar, Amit Kumar Sharma, E.C. Agrawala
legal_representation.state: H.P. Rawal, ASG, A. Mariarputham, Ranjana Narayan, P.K. Dey, A.K. Sharma, Shail Kumar Bhat, B. Krishna Prasad, Anis Suhrawardy, S. Mehndi Imam, Tabrez Ahmad, Mohd. Parvez Dabas

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under s. 3(3) of TADA Act and s. 302 of RPC, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused was part of a conspiracy to eliminate the deceased, who was viewed as an agent of the Indian Government. The accused's confessional statement under Section 15 of the TADA Act was voluntary and truthful, corroborated by oral and documentary evidence, and sufficient to prove the homicidal death of the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence asserted that the accused had not made any confessional statement and that the confession could not be used for non-TADA offences like Section 302 of the RPC. They also claimed that the life sentence imposed was incorrect as the accused could only be held guilty of abetting murder, not committing it.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a voluntary and truthful confession, without the need for corroboration, can solely form the basis of conviction, provided it relates to the accused himself.
precedent_relied_upon: S.N. Dube vs. N.B. Bhoir and Ors. 2000 (2) SCC 254; Ravinder Singh alias Bittu vs. State of Maharashtra 2002 (9) SCC 55; Lakeman Shah and Anr. vs. State of WB. etc. etc. 2001 (5) SCC 235; Abdulvahab Abdul Majid Shaikh and Ors. vs. State of Gujarat etc. etc. 2007 (9) SCC 293; Kartar Singh vs. State of Punjab 1994 (3) SCC 569; State (NCT of Delhi) vs. Navjot Sandhu @ Afsan Guru etc. etc. 2005 (11) SCC 600
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence of life imprisonment was imposed because the accused was found guilty of conspiring and executing a terrorist act, which resulted in the death of the deceased. The court found the confession and corroborating evidence sufficient to justify the conviction and sentence.
